chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The private part (of a man) becomes permissible through three: marriage with inheritance, and marriage without inheritance, and marriage of possession of the right hand (slave girl).

key_terms.الْفَرْجُ: The private part, referring specifically to the male organ in this context of permissibility.
key_terms.بِلَا مِيرَاثٍ: Without inheritance, referring to a marriage where the wife does not inherit (e.g., temporary marriage or specific conditions).
key_terms.بِمِيرَاثٍ: With inheritance, referring to a marriage where the wife inherits from the husband.
key_terms.مِلْكِ الْيَمِينِ: Possession of the right hand, referring to slave girls owned by the man.

ai.seo_question: What are the three ways a man's private part becomes permissible in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi categorizes the three fundamental legal avenues for sexual permissibility in Shia fiqh: permanent marriage (nikah), temporary marriage (mut'ah) which is distinctively Shia and lacks inheritance rights, and ownership of a slave (milk al-yamin). It highlights the jurisprudential nuance that while permanent marriage entails inheritance, the other two mechanisms do not, thereby clarifying the scope of marital rights and obligations within the tradition.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The private parts are Made to be Permissible by three – a marriage by inheritance, and a marriage without inheritance, and a marriage by the possession of the right hand (slave girl)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from af-Nawfafiy from af-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Marriage is of three conditions: It is with right for inheritance, or without the right for inheritance, or it is marriage with the right of ownership.’”
